To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the irradiation of Ti turbidity containing particles in aqueous suspension by γ-radiation generates a significant quantity of radiolytic H2.

(i) γ-radiation of aqueous suspension of titanium metal powder results in significant hydrogen generation and (ii) the yield of hydrogen can be increased manifold by adding methanol to the turbid solution of Ti.

(i) the use of titanium metal turbid solutions in water for hydrogen generation using gamma radiation is an effective method; (ii) the use of Ti turbid solutions with methanol addition is an efficient and effective method for hydrogen generation using γ radiation; and (iii) the Ti turbid solutions can be generated in a simple and inexpensive way using a magnetic stirrer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of Ti turbidity as an efficient scavenger for hydroxyl radicals and its application in hydrogen generation by γ-radiation.
the use of γ-radiolysis for the generation of hydrogen using titanium turbidity as a catalyst.
the development of an economical and efficient method of hydrogen generation using γ-irradiated titanium turbidity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiolysis of Ti turbid solution in the presence of methanol is a promising technique for hydrogen generation.
the radiolytic hydrogen generation is a function of turbidity concentration and dose of γ-radiations.
the present work is a step forward towards the utilization of γ-radiolysis energy for generation of clean and renewable energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γ-radiation is a viable option for large scale hydrogen production.
γ-radiation can be a viable source of hydrogen generation in the presence of Ti metal turbidity.
the present work is a significant step in the direction of developing an economically viable process of hydrogen production from water by γ-radiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of Ti turbidity as a radiolytic hydrogen generation system is a promising alternative to the conventional water radiolysis system.
the use of metal turbidity as a catalyst for hydrogen production is a new concept in radiolytic hydrogen generation.
the Ti metal turbidity is capable of producing hydrogen in large quantity.
